For tasks with an objectively verifiable outcome, a properly constructed checklist decouples these steps. A non-expert panel does not need to 'understand' the domain; it only needs to reliably perceive the presence or absence of binary features. The aggregation of multiple independent perceptors reduces the noise in feature perception (variance), while the checklist's predetermined weighting structure eliminates idiosyncratic feature selection (bias).
